ideas.title: Throw a pot, glaze it, open the kiln
ideas.goal: The player throws a jug on a kick wheel, cuts lines into it with a stick, dips it in glaze and fires it in the kiln by the cottage; when the kiln opens, the jug looks the way they made it: lines they cut fill with darker glaze, a ring they pinched up shows bare clay at its top, a thick dip runs and drips at the foot. Fun because every jug is different and you get better at it: you learn how deep to cut and how long to dip.
ideas.idea: The jug is a lathe profile the player shapes with the mouse while it spins; cuts and pinches change the body's relief. Firing runs a thin-film glaze flow on the GPU (lubrication equation: surface tension levels the molten glaze into grooves, gravity drains it down, it breaks off ridges; I built the solver on a flat patch in my free time and it reproduced a 13th-century celadon pot's darker lines and pale breaks unasked). The fired glaze thickness becomes the jug's material in the path tracer: a clear coat whose colour depth is Beer-Lambert absorption through the simulated thickness. The friends use the jugs (water the garden, carry berries).
ideas.form: A plugin with a wheel, a glaze bucket and a kiln as places on the island, P in Jump in at the wheel; the film is a traced turntable of the first jug coming out of the kiln next to the museum pot that inspired it.

ideas.title: Roast a marshmallow to golden
ideas.goal: At the evening campfire the player holds a marshmallow on a stick over the embers and turns it; too close and it catches fire and blackens, too far and it stays pale, just right and it swells and turns golden all round. Fun because it is a small skill you get good at, and the friends rate yours and want one too.
ideas.idea: Heat flows from the fire as radiation and hot air into a sphere of sugar foam (radial heat conduction, many shells); the crust browns by Maillard and caramelisation kinetics (Arrhenius rate from the literature), the air cells inside expand with temperature so it swells and sags off the stick, and past ignition temperature the surface burns with a flame that chars it. Someone watching sees the colour creep round as you turn it, the puff, and the sudden flare.
ideas.form: A plugin at the campfire (M in Jump in at dusk), the marshmallow's crust colour drawn from the browning field; film: three marshmallows side by side, pale, golden and on fire, traced at dusk lit only by the fire.

ideas.title: Dominoes the friends set up all day
ideas.goal: All afternoon the friends stand wooden blocks on end in a winding line across the meadow, round the lantern and over the bridge; the player tips the first (or a friend knocks one over too early and they groan and rebuild). Fun because the chain runs on real contact: gaps too wide stop it, curves can fail, and the player can redesign the line.
ideas.idea: Each domino is a rigid body in PrintSim (affine bodies, IPC contact) on the GPU: they topple, hit the next, slide and pile up. This is also the test my climbing project needs: a PrintSim body that visibly tips. The friends place them with real gaps they choose (one of them always puts them too far apart).
ideas.form: A plugin that runs the domino scene in the afternoon; a traced film following the falling front along the line, low and close.

ideas.title: Who stole the pie: follow the footprints
ideas.goal: Somebody took the pie from the cottage window; the player follows tracks pressed into the soft ground (whose feet? how fast were they going? where did they stop?) through mud, sand and grass to the thief. Fun because reading tracks is real detective work and every pie theft is different.
ideas.idea: Every creature's feet press into a ground deformation field (a soil yield model: mud keeps deep sharp prints, dry sand slumps them, grass barely shows them); running feet print deeper toes and longer strides, the pie-carrier's prints go deeper from the weight, rain softens and fills them, wind blurs sand prints. The tracks come from the real walk, not drawn.
ideas.form: A height field around the island drawn as a displacement in raster and tracer, a mini game 'Who took the pie'; film: a traced low shot along a line of prints changing from mud to sand.

ideas.title: Sledging down the snow hill on a tea tray
ideas.goal: After a snow night the player sits on a tea tray at the top of the hill and steers down by leaning; the tray carves grooves, packs a track that gets faster each run, and jumps off a bump the friends built. Fun because the track you make changes the next run, and you race the friends.
ideas.idea: The tray is a rigid body sliding on the snow depth field (physics/snow.jl): friction from snow compaction (fresh snow slow, packed track fast), the runner presses the snow down where it passes, leaning shifts weight and turns it. Someone watching sees the track deepen and the runs get faster and wilder.
ideas.form: Plugin on the snow field, a race mini game; film: three runs on the same hill, the track forming.

ideas.title: Push the snowball yourself and build a snowman (snowball project)
ideas.goal: After a night of snow the player, as Lumi, pushes a snowball across the meadow; it packs on the snow it rolls over, gets heavier and harder to push uphill, and they lift one onto another to build a snowman with the friends. Fun because the ball is as big as the path you choose.
ideas.idea: physics/snowball.jl (mass from the snow it eats, Bekker sinkage, rolling inertia) moves from the film script into the game: a snow field over the meadow, the ball pushed by Lumi's real push force, and a ball that rolls into the sea now floats or sinks by its density (the review's finding).
ideas.form: Plugin in Jump in (push with W against the ball), take 2 of the film with a checked camera 3 m from the run.

ideas.title: Giant soap bubbles from a string wand
ideas.goal: The player dips a string wand in a bucket and walks slowly backwards to pull a giant bubble out of it; move too fast and it tears, too slow and it never closes. The bubble drifts, its colours swirl, a black spot opens on top before it pops. Fun because pulling a big one is a skill, and the friends chase them.
ideas.idea: The soap film is a thin film whose thickness drains by gravity and marangoni swirls (the same lubrication equation as my glaze, on a closed surface), and its colours are real thin-film interference in the path tracer (a new Hikari material: reflectance from the simulated thickness per point); the film pops where it thins below ~10 nm. The wand pull is a minimal-surface membrane between the string and the closing neck.
ideas.form: Plugin with a wand and a bucket on the beach; film: a traced close-up at golden hour, the colour bands sliding down until the black spot opens.

ideas.title: Lumi's feathers are real
ideas.goal: Lumi's feathers react to the world: wind ruffles them, rain soaks them so Lumi looks thin and sad and shakes off a spray, cold puffs them out round, and Lumi preens them back. A player sees Lumi's mood and weather in its body. Fun because a character that gets wet and shakes like a dog is the kind of moment people clip.
ideas.idea: Each feather group is a short stiff strand (rods with bending stiffness) on Lumi's body; water adds mass and sticks barbs together (they clump and droop), wind loads them by drag, puffing is a muscle angle. The shake is a real spin-shake: droplets leave at the speed the body turns. My mood file sets how puffed or flat they are.
ideas.form: Engine change to Lumi's body plus a rain reaction; film: Lumi caught in a shower, soaked, shaking, traced.

ideas.title: Sneak past the owl (owl-ears project)
ideas.goal: At night the player, as a small friend, sneaks from the hedge to the berry bush past an owl in a tree. Every step makes a sound, loud on gravel and dry leaves, soft on moss; the owl turns its head to where it heard you and swoops if you were loud. Fun because you learn the ground and your feet.
ideas.idea: physics/echo.jl `hear` already gives the owl first-wavefront hearing; the walk adds step loudness from surface and speed, the owl's head turning to the arrival direction, and a swoop that misses if you freeze.
ideas.form: A mini game at night; film: a traced night sneak seen from behind the owl's head.

ideas.title: The kites tangle
ideas.goal: On a windy day two friends fly kites near each other; the player can fly one too, and the strings cross, wrap and drag both kites down unless you steer them apart. Fun because it is a small fight in the sky that you win by feel.
ideas.idea: Each kite is a rigid sheet with lift and drag from the wind (flat plate aerodynamics), the lines are real ropes (PrintSim rods) that collide with each other and wrap; a wrapped pair loses lift and spirals down.
ideas.form: Plugin on a windy afternoon; film: two kites wrapping and spiralling into the meadow, traced.
